sentence: When you jump, you push the ground away, and the ground is the whole planet.
claim: A jump is a push against the ground; by Newton's third law the ground (the Earth) is pushed the other way with an equal force.
source_title: Conservation of Momentum (HyperPhysics, Georgia State University)
note: Momentum conservation for an isolated system (people + Earth). 'The whole planet': the ground is attached to the Earth, which recoils as one body (rigid-Earth idealisation; badge 'idealised').

sentence: So gather everyone into one crowd, all eight billion, and jump together.
claim: About 8.2 billion people were alive in mid-2024.
source_title: World Population Prospects 2024 (UN DESA Population Division)
note: Said as 'eight billion' (the spine shows 8.2 billion). Gathering everyone in one place is the thought experiment's assumption (badge): spread round the globe, the pushes point in different directions and largely cancel.

sentence: For about half a second we're all in the air, and the planet, pushed the other way, drops away beneath our feet.
claim: A standing jump that raises the body 0.40 m keeps it in the air 0.57 s (t = 2·sqrt(2h/g)); while the people rise, the Earth moves the opposite way so the shared centre of mass stays put.
note: Adult standing-jump norms run about 30-50 cm (Topend Sports' norms: men about 41-50 cm, women 31-40 cm; a study of 116 mostly college-aged adults averaged 45 cm for men and 30 cm for women). calc.py uses 40 cm; 30-50 cm gives 0.49-0.64 s in the air: 'about half a second'. The motion direction: HyperPhysics, conservation of momentum.

sentence: It sounds like it should knock the planet off course.
claim: It does not: the jump is internal to the Earth-plus-people system, so their shared centre of mass, which is what orbits the Sun, does not change course.
source_title: Conservation of Momentum (HyperPhysics, Georgia State University)
note: The sentence states a common intuition; the claim is its correction (the next sentence carries the size). No external force acts, so the centre of mass keeps its orbit; the Earth's body moves only relative to it, by the shift in c6.

sentence: But the push is shared out by weight, and the Earth outweighs all of us ten trillion times over.
claim: 8.2 billion people at 62 kg is 5.1e+11 kg; the Earth is 5.97 × 10^24 kg, 1.2e+13 times more: about ten trillion (10^13) times.
note: Earth's mass 5.9722 × 10^24 kg (NASA fact sheet). 62 kg: the world's average adult mass (Walpole et al. 2012, https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2458-12-439); children weigh less, so all of us weigh less than 5.1 × 10^11 kg and the ratio is, if anything, larger. 'Shared out by weight': equal and opposite momenta, so each side's velocity is inversely proportional to its mass.

sentence: So the whole planet moves a distance three thousand times smaller than a single atom.
claim: The Earth's shift is N·m·h/M = 3.4e-14 m (shown '≈ 3 × 10^-14 m'); a hydrogen atom is about 2 Bohr radii, 1.06e-10 m, across: 3,108 times wider, said as three thousand.
note: Bohr radius 5.29177210544 × 10^-11 m (CODATA 2022). Hydrogen is the smallest atom, so 'a single atom' is the conservative comparison: larger atoms make the ratio bigger. Computed in calc.py.

sentence: And when we land, it settles right back where it was.
claim: Landing reverses the jump: the people's momentum returns to the Earth, and with the centre of mass fixed the Earth ends where it began.
source_title: Conservation of Momentum (HyperPhysics, Georgia State University)
note: Idealised (rigid Earth, no energy lost to sound or heat changes nothing about the positions). The scene shows the Earth back at its mark.

sentence: Jump higher, or count us lighter, and it stays thousands of times smaller than an atom.
claim: Sensitivity: jump 0.30-0.50 m: an atom is 2,487-4,144 times wider than the shift; everyone at half the mass: 6,216 times; 10 billion people jumping 0.5 m: 2,039 times. Every case: thousands.
note: calc.py sensitivity table; the show-your-work card shows the rows.

sentence: So yes, the Earth moves when we jump.
claim: The shift is not zero: about 3e-14 m while we are in the air.
note: Restates c6 in words; 'never notices' (the next sentence, no claim) is figurative.
